title: Modeling the Bad Property: 'Value j Is Missed'
content: `missSet n j` is the set of functions Fin n → Fin k that miss the value j (no input maps to j) — the j-th 'bad property' over the universe of all functions. This is the modeling choice that lets the parent's general dual sieve apply verbatim with the ground type instantiated to a function type. `inf_missSet_eq_filter` identifies the intersection of the miss-sets over a value set t with the functions whose every output avoids t, repackaging an intersection of bad properties as a single value-avoidance condition ready to be counted.
mathContext: $\mathrm{missSet}(j)=\{f\mid\forall i,\ f(i)\neq j\}$; $\bigsqcap_{j\in t}\mathrm{missSet}(j)=\{f\mid\forall i,\ f(i)\notin t\}$.

title: The Crux Count: (k − |t|)ⁿ Value-Avoiding Functions
content: `card_missesOn` — the one piece of real counting. The functions Fin n → Fin k missing every value of a set t number exactly (k − |t|)^n, because such a function is precisely a function into the complementary (k − |t|)-element codomain Fin k \ t. The proof builds the explicit equivalence {f // ∀ i, f i ∉ t} ≃ (Fin n → {x : Fin k // x ∉ t}) (toFun/invFun by component projection), then applies Fintype.card_fun (|β^α| = |β|^|α|) and Fintype.card_subtype_compl (the complement subtype has k − |t| elements). Everything else in the file is bookkeeping around this count.
mathContext: $\#\{f:\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to\mathrm{Fin}\,k\mid\forall i,\ f(i)\notin t\}=(k-|t|)^n$ via $\{f\mid f\text{ avoids }t\}\simeq(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to(\mathrm{Fin}\,k\setminus t))$.

title: The Avoid Set Is Exactly the Surjections
content: `avoid_eq_filter_surjective`: the sieve's 'avoid' set — the functions lying in NONE of the missSet n j — equals the set of surjective functions Fin n → Fin k. The reasoning is the tautology that missing no value is the same as hitting every value: ¬(∃ j, value j missed) ⟺ ∀ j, ∃ i, f i = j ⟺ Function.Surjective f (closed by push_neg and tauto). This structural identification is what makes the abstract sieve compute the surjection count — the avoid set's cardinality IS the number of surjections.
mathContext: $\bigsqcap_j\mathrm{missSet}(j)^c=\{f\mid f\text{ surjective}\}$: missing no value $\iff$ hitting every value.

title: The Closed Sieve Form of the Surjection Count
content: `card_surjective_eq_sieve_sum`: #(surjections Fin n → Fin k) = Σ_{j=0}^k (-1)^j C(k,j)(k-j)^n. The proof applies the parent's general dual sieve `InclusionExclusionSieve.card_avoid_sieve` to (univ : Finset (Fin k)) with the bad properties missSet n, rewriting the avoid set as the surjections. The resulting alternating powerset sum Σ_{t⊆univ}(-1)^|t| |⋂ missSet| is then grouped by subset size via `Finset.powerset_card_disjiUnion`: every subset t of size j contributes (-1)^j(k-j)^n (by inf_missSet_eq_filter + card_missesOn), and there are C(k,j) such subsets (`card_powersetCard`), so the inner sum collapses to C(k,j)(-1)^j(k-j)^n and ring finishes. This is the textbook inclusion–exclusion formula, derived as a genuine instance of a reusable theorem.
relatedConcepts: Stirling numbers of the second kind

title: Axiom-Free Concrete Check: 6 Surjections [3] ↠ [2]
content: The general formula is specialised to n = 3, k = 2 (via card_surjective_eq_sieve_sum 3 2) and the sieve sum is evaluated: Σ_{j=0}^2 (-1)^j C(2,j)(2-j)^3 = 8 − 2 + 0 = 6, matching the 2³ − 2 = 6 surjections of a 3-set onto a 2-set. The evaluation uses `decide` (kernel reduction), NOT `native_decide`, so the worked example introduces no Lean.ofReduceBool axiom and the file remains genuinely axiom-free (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
